title: OAuth Assist for HA - provider profile (v2)
description: Declares which login pages and redirect URIs the extension watches for one provider. Profiles never configure a forward destination: captured codes only ever go to https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/oauth. Nor do they configure where Home Assistant hands over its routing token: that sentinel URL is a constant in the extension.

schemaVersion.description: 1 is the original redirect-only profile. 2 adds the "initiation" capture step and the "stashed" state rule.

id.description: Short unique slug for the provider, e.g. "acme-app".

name.description: Human-readable provider name shown in the UI.

items.description: An https match pattern (e.g. "https://login.acme-app.com/*"). Enabling the profile requests a runtime host permission for each pattern.

capture.description: Capture steps. Exactly one "redirect" step is required. An optional "initiation" step (schemaVersion 2) must come first, and requires state.rule "stashed".

items.description: URL prefix to intercept: a custom-scheme URI (e.g. "com.acme.app://") or an https prefix (e.g. "https://login.acme-app.com/ios/"). http://, my.home-assistant.io, and the extension's own sentinel scheme are rejected.

oneOf.description: Declares that Home Assistant hands this provider's routing token (state_HA) to the extension BEFORE login, because the provider's callback state is opaque (e.g. ciphertext) and cannot be recognized as a Home Assistant flow. Carries no URLs and no parameter names on purpose: the sentinel URL is a constant in the extension, and the parameter names are fixed. There is nothing here to point at a hostile destination.

ttlSeconds.description: How long a stashed pending flow stays usable. Single-use, and bound to the tab and profile that created it.

rule.description: "ha-jwt": auto-forward only when state is a Home Assistant flow JWT (contains flow_id). "none": forward whenever code and state are present. "stashed" (schemaVersion 2): the callback's state is opaque; forward the state_HA stashed by the "initiation" step instead, and never forward the provider's own state. Requires an "initiation" step, and vice versa.
